Worm Plot of the Residuals

Source: R/plot_diagnostic.R
plot_worm.Rd

Selects the detrended quantile-quantile graph of the quantile residuals: the difference between each sorted residual and its theoretical quantile, against the theoretical quantile, with the band of plot_qq() detrended in the same way. With over, the observations are divided into classes of a covariate and one worm is drawn for each class.

Usage

plot_worm(
  over = NULL,
  n_inter = 4,
  band = "order",
  level = 0.95,
  n_sim = 99,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

over

The name of a covariate, or NULL.

n_inter

The number of classes of a numeric covariate.

band, level, n_sim, seed

See plot_qq().

Value

A PlotWorm object, inheriting from diagnostic_plot.

Details

A worm plot (van Buuren and Fredriks, 2001) turns the departures from the line of the quantile-quantile graph into departures from the horizontal axis. An intercept different from zero shows a wrong mean of the residuals, a slope a wrong variance, a U shape a wrong skewness and an S shape a wrong kurtosis. With over a numeric covariate is divided into n_inter classes of equal count (a factor into its levels), which requires data in autoplot.StatmodFit(). The band is that of plot_qq() computed within each class.

References

van Buuren, S. and Fredriks, M. (2001). Worm plot: a simple diagnostic device for modelling growth reference curves. Statistics in Medicine 20(8), 1259–1277.

See also

plot_qq(), plot_calibration(), diagnostics()

Examples

set.seed(1)
dd <- data.frame(x = runif(160))
dd$y <- 1 + dd$x + rnorm(160, sd = 0.4)
fit <- statmod(y ~ x, distributions7::gaussian1_distrib(), dd)
ggplot2::autoplot(fit, plot_type = plot_worm())

ggplot2::autoplot(fit, plot_type = plot_worm(over = "x", n_inter = 3), data = dd)
